mission: Admiral Klauskin in his flagship cabin — combat-stress symptoms surface; he speaks to the chair his dead wife used to sit in.
why_now: The fleet is en route to Corellian space; the command load is now constant.
opening_hook: Klauskin alone in his cabin with a cold tea and a chair angled toward an empty seat.
conflict: Klauskin's professional self-image against the grief that the command load is cracking open.
turning_point: Klauskin speaks aloud to his dead wife — the first on-page break in his professional composure.
closing_hook: Klauskin putting the tea down beside the empty chair.
setting: Flagship cabin, Alliance command cruiser en route to Corellian space.
sensory_details: Cold tea smell; the cabin's dimmed lighting; the chair angled toward the empty seat.
emotional_trajectory: Professional isolation → grief leak → whispered exchange with the absent.

stakes.interpersonal: Klauskin's relationship with his dead wife continuing in hallucinated form.

action_beats: He sets down the cold tea
He speaks to the empty chair
notes: The book's cleanest single-character interior collapse scene.
